text.p: Salomon Brothers in London has downgraded its rating of Polish construction company Budimex SA from buy to hold saying the company's 1997 earnings had not been satisfactory, Salomon said in a report.
"We are downgrading our recommendation on Budimex from a 'buy' to a 'hold' in light of recent disappointing earnings," the report dated August 12 said.
Last month the firm revised down its 1997 group pre-tax profit forecast to 23 million zlotys from the earlier forecast 33.7 million and parent pre-tax to 15 million zlotys from 25.7 million.
It revised down its 1997 group net profit forecast to 18 million zlotys from 28 million and parent net to 13 million from 23.5 million.

Budimex said it had made the revisions in part due to a downturn of the business cycle on the German and Czech markets, flooding in the Czech Republic and limited sales in the Commonwealth of Independent States.

Salomon said Budimex's unconsolidated net profit would reach 11.7 million zlotys in 1997 and consolidated net profit 18 million. It said that in 1998 the two numbers should rise to 15.5 million zlotys and 22 million zlotys respectively.
